properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 is used for hashing in shadowsocks configuration and release scripts. This is a known insecure algorithm that is vulnerable to collision attacks.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CTR, CFB, and OFB modes are used in shadowsocks configurations. These modes do not provide authenticated encryption and are vulnerable to malleability attacks unless a separate MAC is applied.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Poly1305 is used in shadowsocks and vmess configurations as an authenticator. While the algorithm itself is secure, its usage context suggests legacy crypto configurations.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Static IVs/nonce values are used in vmess AEAD configurations, which can lead to catastrophic security failures when the same key is reused.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-224 is used in trojan configuration. While better than SHA-1, it's a weakened variant of SHA-2 and not recommended for cryptographic use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Non-constant time comparison is used in vmess server for MAC verification, which can leak timing information and be vulnerable to side-channel attacks.
